chunks.title: Who I am
chunks.body: I'm Anggie Putra Dimasta, a Staff Software Engineer in Jakarta, Indonesia. I'm currently a Platform Engineer Frontend at Lion Parcel, a logistics and courier service. I focus on high-level system architecture, set technical standards, and build AI-driven internal tools to optimize developer workflows. I've been shipping software professionally since 2012 and doing frontend and platform engineering since 2016.

chunks.title: The SDLC engine I maintain
chunks.body: At Lion Parcel I catalyzed this one and still help maintain it — an orchestration layer that turns generic AI coding assistants into domain-expert partners. It ships specialized agents, context-aware commands, and project-specific rules, installed into consuming repositories with a single command. The agent skill set is defined once as a source of truth and symlinked into every supported editor, so a change propagates everywhere instead of being copied per tool.

chunks.title: How I actually spend my time
chunks.body:
My leverage as a Staff engineer is mostly in making work buildable before it gets written. I do that systematically - detailing, grooming and breaking requirements down until they are implementation-ready - so the ambiguity surfaces while it is still cheap to fix. 

Over the last fifteen months that came to roughly 2,900 story points across 976 tickets and about 2,400 logged hours - most of it specification work, with the features built by the engineers those specs went to. That discipline is the part of my job I am most proud of. A well-shaped ticket is worth more than a fast commit, and the documentation that comes out of it outlives the sprint.

chunks.title: Docs as engineering infrastructure
chunks.body:
I catalyzed this one too and still look after it: a documentation-first workspace that bridges Jira epics and PRDs with technical implementation. Its core is a living record of: service ownership, API contracts, database schemas, domain terminology, and UI-to-API mappings — kept current as a source of truth and updated as the services change. 

On top of that sits a command suite that turns requirements into implementation-ready artifacts, with guards that keep the documentation and the tickets in sync. I co-author our Technical Requirements Document and Functional Specification Document frameworks to set core technical standards and make handover seamless.

chunks.title: Clean Architecture in Vue
chunks.body: Our internal content management platform follows Clean Architecture — Domain, Data, and App layers — deliberately adapted for Vue and TypeScript. The App layer holds dependency injection, repositories, and routing with permission logic; Data holds payload contracts and mappers between API shapes and domain types; Domain holds entities and use cases. I own 48 pull requests in that codebase. The lesson is that a layered architecture in a frontend app is about keeping the UI from knowing where data comes from, not about ceremony.

chunks.title: Koltiva — Frontend Engineer
chunks.body: From December 2021 to February 2025 I was a Frontend Engineer at Koltiva, an agritech company providing end-to-end supply chain solutions for traceability, sustainability, and farmer engagement. I built and maintained 5 web applications across several product lines - payments, traceability, farm retail, and recruitment - with Vue.js, Nuxt, TypeScript, Pinia, and TailwindCSS, and built and maintained 3 UI component libraries. I contributed to the shared Nuxt starter the team bootstrapped new projects from - it exists to scaffold microfrontends, so a good part of it is about keeping independently deployed apps sharing dependencies cleanly. I worked with backend and UI/UX designers to ship features, applying modular and scalable frontend architecture.

chunks.title: Backend and API work
chunks.body:
My production backend work comes from my own projects: Go Fiber, FastAPI, Express, tRPC, PHP, and background workers using the outbox pattern. Most of those were exploratory - built to find out whether an approach held up, which is a different thing from running a business on it. The exception is Hesoyam, which I use every day, running on a small service mesh with PostgreSQL row-level security.

At Lion Parcel I own the frontend and the internal tooling, and integrate against the Go services the platform team runs.
